data_fields.name: combo_window_per_step
data_fields.donor_constant: start < t <= end, ms from clip start; values come from the clip's COMBO_WINDOW frames / fps

data_fields.name: hit_end_per_step
data_fields.donor_constant: ms from HIT_END event frames / fps

data_fields.name: parry_window
data_fields.donor_constant: start <= t < end, ms from PARRY_FRAME frames / fps

data_fields.name: crossfade_window
data_fields.donor_constant: max(blend out, blend in); each file value x 1000

best_idea: Each attack clip carries its own combo windows and hit-end times, converted from frames to ms with its frame rate; a follow-up swing counts only inside the current step's window, and a successful chain rewinds the clock to that step's hit end.
decision_why: Take the window-gated chain and the hit-end rewind, but keep the windows as catalogue data the server reads (rows 20-21), not client clip events. The client only plays the clip. The server must store the step index and its own start time, not rewrite a shared clock. The per-clip values are catalogue fields; engine constant is the nearest schema option.
acceptance: In a duel a second swing is accepted only when its press falls inside the step's window from the catalogue; outside it, a fresh swing starts (or the combo breaks for the same attack). A server test asserts the same accept or reject on the server copy of the windows.
